title: The Tent Count
hook: The ranger at Pine Hollow had one rule: if your tent zipper opens after the fire's out, don't sit up. Just count heads.
lines: The summer after graduation, my three best friends and I went camping at Pine Hollow.
The old ranger counted us at the gate... and gave us one rule.
If you hear your tent zipper open after the fire's out... don't sit up. Don't turn on a light. Just count heads, in the dark.
We joked about it all through dinner.
Marco kept zipping the tent open and shut, just to make Jess scream.
Then the fire burned down to coals... and the four of us squeezed into one small tent.
Sometime after two, I woke up. Everyone was breathing slow.
And then I heard it. The zipper. Opening... one tooth at a time.
Cold air slid across my face. Something crawled in... and lay down, very carefully, beside me.
I didn't sit up. I reached out in the dark, and counted.
Four. Everyone was here. Everyone was asleep.
Then, right beside my ear... a soft voice kept counting.
